claim: I-complete-diagnostic-on-first-pass faithfully states Akien's proven method: a diagnostic surface delivers all data required to resolve the issue in its initial emission, and the resolver never re-runs the thing to gather more.
method: quorum signature gate — review by 1 reader(s), quorum 1; verdict = the reviewers', seal recorded by notary 'cc' (different hands)

signatures.restated: AKIEN'S OWN WORDS, VERBATIM (2026-07-23, the message that cast the piece): "when i built that test automation framework, i knew we would have errors. and we'd need to fix them. and all too often i'd have to run things over and over and over again gathering additional failure data. so i built the framework to deliver EVERYTHING I would need on the first pass. we talk about that same model in UU and i think we've talked here about Trouble Tickets. A trouble ticket is a system alarm THAT DELIVERS ALL THE DIAGNOSTIC DATA REQUIRED TO RESOLVE THE ISSUE IN THE INITIAL REPORT. Same idea. So this is not an unproven idea. This is the very first tool i reach for in debugging. validated by experience. i take teams that can take half a day to solve an issue and bring that down to 10 minutes. so yeah, proven." He supplied the 2007 framework's actual report format as the worked example (short_name, file, line, code, description, result, expected_value, actual_value, failed_is_fatal, source, stack_trace) — which is the field list the piece names and the inspector seeds. || THIS IS A REVIEW, NOT ONLY AN ORIGIN. The piece is CC's restatement of Akien's method, and he read it and CORRECTED IT TWICE; both corrections were incorporated before this seal. (1) 'I am ok with that... but... that rule is for speculative ideas' — build-minimal / grow-against-need does NOT gate a decades-proven tool, so the piece must say it is built ahead of need. (2) 'almost... this is a special class of falsifier, so worth discussing... if a diagnostic forces a second run to resolve some additional point, that's an immediate learning signal for next time' — a forced second run is NOT a terminal refutation, so the falsifier was split into learned (feed-forward) vs recurred (terminal). A reviewer who reads, disagrees, states why, and whose objection changes the artifact has reviewed it.

falsifier: Akien reads the sealed text and says the restatement is NOT faithful — which appends a RED beside this green and kicks the piece back to the point of creation (CP2). The trail is append-only, so this seal is overturned by a later verdict, never by an edit. SPECIFIC TO THIS SEAL: the verdict is read from Akien's verbatim statements of 2026-07-23 on the record, not collected fresh on 2026-07-25; if he holds that his two recorded corrections do not amount to a review of the final text, this seal is void.
